questions.question: Which city was chosen to host a major five-day Sumo wrestling tournament in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**London, UK**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The city of **London**, **United Kingdom**, has been officially chosen to host a major five-day **Sumo** wrestling tournament in **October 2025**.
 
• This landmark event, titled "**Grand Sumo London**," is scheduled to take place at the **O2 Arena**, one of the world's most popular music and entertainment venues.
 
• The tournament marks the first time in over **30 years** that the **Japan Sumo Association** has brought a full-scale professional sumo event to **London**; the last occurrence was in **1991** at the **Royal Albert Hall**.
 
• The **five-day** event in **2025** will feature approximately **70 professional rikishi** (wrestlers) traveling from **Japan** to compete.
 
• The roster of participants is expected to include the sport's highest-ranking athletes, including the **Yokozuna** (grand champion) and **Ozeki** (champion), providing a rare opportunity for international fans to witness the elite level of the sport. ***Hence, the correct answer is London, UK.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of Sumo Ranking:**
 
 
• The **Banzuke** is the official hierarchy of sumo wrestlers. The top division is known as **Makuuchi**, which contains a fixed number of **42 wrestlers**.
 
• The **Yokozuna** is the pinnacle of the sport; unlike other ranks, a **Yokozuna** cannot be demoted for a poor performance but is expected to retire if they can no longer compete at the highest level.
 
• Other high ranks include **Ozeki**, **Sekiwake**, and **Komusubi**, collectively referred to as the **Sanyaku**.
 
 
 
• **The Playing Area (Dohyo):**
 
 
• Sumo matches take place in a **Dohyo**, a circular ring made of specialized **clay** and covered with a thin layer of sand.
 
• The ring is exactly **4.55 meters** in diameter and is defined by **tawara** (rice-straw bales) buried in the clay.
 
• A wrestler loses the match if any part of his body other than the soles of his feet touches the ground, or if he is pushed outside the circle of the **tawara**.
 
 
 
• **Tournament Types:**
 
 
• Official tournaments, called **Honbasho**, occur **six times a year** in **Japan** (three in **Tokyo**, and one each in **Osaka**, **Nagoya**, and **Fukuoka**).
 
• The **London 2025** event is classified as a **Jungyo** (exhibition tour), which aims to promote the sport and engage with fans outside the standard competitive season.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** The **1991** tournament in **London** was a pivotal moment for the sport's global visibility, marking the first time a **sumo tournament** was held outside **Japan** in its **1,500-year history**.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** Sumo is deeply rooted in **Shinto** traditions. Rituals such as **Shiko** (leg stomping to drive away evil spirits) and the throwing of **salt** (to purify the ring) are integral parts of the pre-match ceremony.
 
• **Match Duration:** While the rituals and preparation can take several minutes, the actual bout typically lasts only **10 to 60 seconds**, emphasizing explosive power and technique.
 
• **Governing Body:** All professional sumo is overseen by the **Japan Sumo Association (Nihon Sumo Kyokai)**, based in **Ryogoku**, **Tokyo**.
</ul

questions.question: In 2025, which institution was directed by the National Green Tribunal to assess the ultraviolet sewage treatment technology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IIT Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, the **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** issued a significant directive to the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi** to conduct an expert assessment of **Ultraviolet (UV) radiation technology** used in **Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs)**.
 
• The primary objective of this assessment is to evaluate the **germicidal efficacy** of UV systems in neutralizing harmful pathogens, such as **fecal coliform**, which often persist in treated sewage water before it is discharged into rivers like the **Yamuna** and **Ganga**. ***Hence, the correct option is IIT Delhi.***
 
• The **NGT**, led by its **Chairperson**, emphasized the need for a scientific audit because many **STPs** across India were failing to meet the **permissible limits** of bacterial contamination despite using UV disinfection.
 
• The study by **IIT Delhi** is expected to provide a comparative analysis between **UV treatment** and other disinfection methods like **chlorination** or **ozonation** to determine the most environmentally sustainable and cost-effective solution for **wastewater management**.
 
• This directive is part of a broader judicial push to refine **environmental standards** and ensure that technical specifications of **urban infrastructure** align with the **Right to a Clean Environment** under **Article 21** of the **Constitution of India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Green Tribunal (NGT):**
 
 
• Established on **18th October 2010** under the **National Green Tribunal Act, 2010**, it is a specialized body for the effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to **environmental protection** and conservation of forests.
 
• The **Principal Bench** of the **NGT** is located in **New Delhi**, with regional benches in **Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, and Chennai**.
 
• It is not bound by the procedure laid down under the **Code of Civil Procedure, 1908**, but is guided by principles of **natural justice**.
 
 
 
• **UV Sewage Treatment Technology:**
 
 
• **UV-C radiation** (specifically wavelengths between **200 and 280 nanometers**) is used to disrupt the **DNA** and **RNA** of microorganisms, preventing them from reproducing.
 
• It is considered a **chemical-free** alternative to chlorine, ensuring that no harmful **disinfection by-products (DBPs)** are introduced into the water ecosystem.
 
• However, the efficiency of **UV systems** is highly dependent on **water turbidity**; suspended solids can shield bacteria from the light, necessitating the expert review ordered in **2025**.
 
 
 
• **IIT Delhi's Role in Policy:**
 
 
• As one of the **Institutes of Eminence**, **IIT Delhi** frequently collaborates with the **Ministry of Jal Shakti** and the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** on projects like the **National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG)**.
 
• The institution’s **Department of Civil Engineering** houses specialized labs for **Environmental Engineering**, making it the preferred technical advisor for **NGT** mandates regarding **sanitation** and **pollution control**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Water Quality Standards:** According to **CPCB** guidelines, the **Fecal Coliform** level in treated sewage should ideally be less than **100 MPN/100ml** for safe discharge into water bodies.
 
• **River Rejuvenation:** The **NGT’s** 2025 order is a critical step in the **Yamuna Rejuvenation Plan**, aiming to stop the "frothing" caused by untreated surfactants and high bacterial loads in **Delhi** and **Agra**.
 
• **Technological Challenges:** While **IIT Kanpur** and **IIT Bombay** also conduct water research, the **NGT** chose **IIT Delhi** due to its proximity to the **Yamuna River STPs** and its ongoing technical monitoring of **Delhi’s** drainage systems.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Bakshi Cup 2025** was the **10th edition** of the Inter-Academy Sports Meet, a prestigious event that brings together the premier officer training institutions of India.
 
• The **Indian Military Academy (IMA)**, located in **Dehradun**, hosted the 2025 edition of the tournament from **6th February to 11th February 2025**.
 
• The **Indian Military Academy (IMA)** emerged as the overall winner of the **Bakshi Cup 2025**, reclaiming the trophy on its home turf.
 
• The **National Defence Academy (NDA)**, situated in **Khadakwasla, Pune**, secured the position of the **runner-up** in the competition after a neck-and-neck struggle for points in the final tally. ***Hence, the correct option is National Defence Academy (NDA).***
 
• The tournament featured participation from five major academies: **IMA Dehradun**, **NDA Khadakwasla**, **Indian Naval Academy (INA) Ezhimala**, **Air Force Academy (AFA) Dundigal**, and **Officers' Training Academy (OTA) Chennai**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bakshi Cup Overview:**
 
 
• The **Bakshi Cup** was instituted in the memory of **Lieutenant General P.S. Bakshi**, a former **Commandant of the IMA**, to promote sportsmanship and healthy competition among trainee officers.
 
• It serves as a platform for **Gentleman Cadets (GCs)** and **Flight Cadets** to exhibit their physical prowess, teamwork, and leadership qualities.
 
• The competition traditionally includes disciplines such as **Cross Country**, **Boxing**, **Football**, **Basketball**, **Hockey**, and **Volleyball**.
 
 
 
• **Participating Academies Details:**
 
 
• **Indian Military Academy (IMA):** Founded in **1932** in **Dehradun, Uttarakhand**, it is the oldest army training academy in India. Its motto is **"Veerta Aur Vivek"** (Valour and Wisdom).
 
• **National Defence Academy (NDA):** Established in **1954** at **Khadakwasla, Maharashtra**, it is the first **tri-service academy** in the world, training cadets for the Army, Navy, and Air Force together. Its motto is **"Seva Parmo Dharma"** (Service Before Self).
 
• **Air Force Academy (AFA):** Located in **Dundigal, Hyderabad**, it was established in **1969** and began operations in **1971**. It provides training to all personnel of the **Indian Air Force**.
 
• **Officers' Training Academy (OTA) Chennai:** Established in **1963**, it focuses on training officers for the **Short Service Commission (SSC)** in the Indian Army.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In the 2025 edition, the **Cross Country** race, often considered the most grueling and decisive event of the meet, saw intense competition between **IMA** and **NDA** cadets.
 
• The **Bakshi Cup** is held biennially or annually depending on the training schedule and rotates its hosting rights among the participating academies.
 
• The **10th edition** in **2025** emphasized the integration of **modern sports technology** and rigorous physical standards required for future military leaders.
 
• Winning the **Bakshi Cup** is considered a matter of immense pride for the academies, reflecting the quality of physical training and the competitive spirit of the **cadets**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the aim of the Digital Twin with AI-Driven Insights initiative showcased at India Mobile Congress 2025?

options.text: To create gaming systems for telecom users
To produce sensors for consumer devices
To design marketing tools for phone makers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To plan and manage infrastructure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Digital Twin with AI-Driven Insights** initiative is a sophisticated technological framework designed to create high-fidelity **virtual replicas** of physical assets, systems, or processes to **plan and manage infrastructure** effectively.
 
• At the **India Mobile Congress 2025**, this initiative highlights the integration of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Internet of Things (IoT)** to provide real-time monitoring and predictive analytics for large-scale projects.
 
• It allows urban planners and engineers to simulate various environmental and operational conditions, helping to optimize the layout of **telecom towers**, **power grids**, and **transportation networks** before physical construction begins. ***Hence, the objective is to plan and manage infrastructure.***
 
• By leveraging **AI-driven insights**, the system can identify potential bottlenecks or structural weaknesses in **utility networks**, thereby enhancing the **resilience** and **sustainability** of national infrastructure.
 
• This initiative is central to the development of **Smart Cities** in **India**, providing a data-centric approach to managing resources and reducing **operational costs** through automated decision-making processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Digital Twin Technology:**
 
 
• A **Digital Twin** is a dynamic virtual model that stays linked to its physical counterpart through **sensors** and **real-time data** feeds.
 
• It is widely used in **Industry 4.0**, **aerospace**, and **automotive sectors** for performance testing and troubleshooting without risking physical hardware.
 
• In the context of **telecommunications**, it helps in mapping **signal coverage** and managing the deployment of **5G and 6G small cells** in dense urban areas.
 
 
 
• **India Mobile Congress (IMC):**
 
 
• **IMC** is the largest **digital technology forum** in **Asia**, jointly organized by the **Department of Telecommunications (DoT)** and the **Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI)**.
 
• The event serves as a platform for showcasing innovations in **6G**, **Artificial Intelligence**, **Cloud Computing**, and **Cybersecurity**.
 
• The **2025 edition** focuses on the theme of "Global Digital Innovation," emphasizing **India's** role as a global leader in **digital transformation**.
 
 
 
• **Role of AI in Infrastructure:**
 
 
• **AI algorithms** process massive datasets generated by infrastructure sensors to perform **predictive maintenance**, identifying faults before they lead to service outages.
 
• This technology is vital for **disaster management**, as it can simulate the impact of **floods** or **earthquakes** on the physical infrastructure of a city.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Applications:**
 
 
• **Network Optimization**: Telecom operators use digital twins to minimize **latency** and maximize **bandwidth** efficiency across **broadband networks**.
 
• **Cost Reduction**: By identifying inefficiencies in the planning stage, the government and private entities can save billions in **capital expenditure (CAPEX)** and **operational expenditure (OPEX)**.
 
• **Data Sovereignty**: As these twins handle sensitive geographical and structural data, the initiative also emphasizes **data security** and compliance with **India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act (2023)**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In June 2025, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) imposed a monetary penalty of ₹29.60 lakh (Rupees Twenty Nine Lakh Sixty Thousand only) on which of the following institutions for non-compliance with certain directions issued by RBI on ‘Licensing of Payments Banks’ on 6 June 2025?

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, by an order dated **June 6, 2025**, has imposed a monetary penalty of **₹29.60 lakh** (Rupees Twenty Nine Lakh Sixty Thousand only) on **Fino Payments Bank Limited**.
 
• The penalty has been imposed in the exercise of powers vested in **RBI** under the provisions of **Section 47A(1)(c)** read with **Section 46(4)(i)** of the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**.
 
• The action was taken due to the bank's non-compliance with certain directions issued by **RBI** on **‘Licensing of Payments Banks’**.
 
• This regulatory action is based on deficiencies in **statutory and regulatory compliance** and is not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the bank with its customers.
 
• The **RBI** had conducted a statutory inspection for **Supervisory Evaluation** of the bank, which revealed violations related to the specific operating guidelines prescribed for **Payments Banks** in **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fino Payments Bank Limited:**
 
 
• It was incorporated on **April 4, 2017**, after receiving the final license from the **Reserve Bank of India**.
 
• The bank is headquartered in **Navi Mumbai**, **Maharashtra**.
 
• **Fino Payments Bank** emerged from **Fino Paytech Limited**, which was a pioneer in the **Business Correspondent (BC)** model for **Financial Inclusion**.
 
• The bank focuses on providing digital banking and payment services to the unbanked and under-banked population across **India**.
 
 
 
• **Payments Banks in India:**
 
 
• These are a specialized category of banks conceptualized by the **RBI** to further **Financial Inclusion**.
 
• They can accept **demand deposits** (currently up to **₹2 lakh** per individual customer) but are prohibited from lending or issuing credit cards.
 
• They mainly provide services such as **ATM/Debit cards**, **mobile banking**, **online fund transfers**, and **third-party insurance** products.
 
• Important examples include **Airtel Payments Bank**, **India Post Payments Bank**, and **Paytm Payments Bank**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework:**
 
 
• The **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, provides the legal framework for the regulation and supervision of the banking sector in **India**.
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, established on **April 1, 1935**, under the **RBI Act, 1934**, serves as the primary regulator for all scheduled commercial banks, including **Payments Banks**.
 
• Penalties are typically issued after a **Show Cause Notice (SCN)** is sent to the institution, and their oral or written submissions are considered by the **Central Bank**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **₹29.60 lakh** penalty highlights the **RBI's** stringent oversight regarding the **Licensing of Payments Banks** guidelines to ensure the stability of the **financial system**.
 
• Compliance with **RBI** directives is mandatory for all financial entities to prevent **operational risks** and maintain **customer trust**.

questions.question: How does the Mizzo Endo 4000, launched in 2025, improve clinical outcomes compared to conventional laparoscopic procedures?

options.text: It reduces dependence on imported robotic surgical systems by enabling indigenous precision surgeries.
It allows large-scale production of low-cost prosthetics through additive manufacturing.
It enhances diagnostic accuracy by integrating AI into pathology workflows.
It improves drug absorption in human tissues using nanotechnology-based delivery systems.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It reduces dependence on imported robotic surgical systems by enabling indigenous precision surgeries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mizzo Endo 4000**, launched in **2025**, is a groundbreaking **indigenous robotic surgical system** developed to enhance the precision and accessibility of minimally invasive surgeries.
 
• Unlike **conventional laparoscopic procedures**, which rely on **2D imaging** and rigid hand-held instruments, the **Mizzo Endo 4000** provides surgeons with **high-definition 3D visualization** and superior **degrees of freedom** for instrument movement.
 
• One of its primary clinical advantages is the integration of **tremor filtration technology**, which ensures that even the most minute **precision surgeries** are performed with extreme accuracy, reducing the risk of accidental tissue damage. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The system significantly lowers **healthcare costs** by providing a domestic alternative to expensive, **imported robotic platforms** like the **Da Vinci** system, making advanced surgery available to a larger demographic.
 
• While **additive manufacturing** is a revolutionary field, it pertains to **3D printing** and prosthetics rather than the active surgical navigation provided by this system. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Mizzo Endo 4000** is designed for **intra-operative** surgical assistance, not for **pathology workflows** or **diagnostic AI** integration. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The device does not involve **nanotechnology-based drug delivery**, which is a pharmacological advancement rather than a mechanical surgical innovation. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Robotic-Assisted Surgery (RAS):**
 
 
• **RAS** is an evolution of **Minimally Invasive Surgery (MIS)** that allows doctors to perform many types of complex procedures with more precision, flexibility, and control than is possible with conventional techniques.
 
• The **Mizzo Endo 4000** utilizes a **master-slave architecture** where the surgeon operates from a console, translating hand movements into micro-movements of robotic arms inside the patient.
 
 
 
• **Indigenous Innovation in Med-Tech:**
 
 
• The launch of indigenous systems in **2025** aligns with the **"Make in India"** initiative, aiming to achieve **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) in the medical device sector.
 
• Reducing reliance on **imported systems** is critical because imported robots often come with high **maintenance contracts** and expensive **disposable instruments** that drive up the cost of surgery.
 
 
 
• **Clinical Outcomes:**
 
 
• Clinical data suggests that robotic platforms lead to **shorter hospital stays**, **reduced blood loss**, and **faster recovery times** compared to open or even standard laparoscopic surgeries.
 
• The **ergonomic design** of the **Mizzo Endo 4000** also reduces **surgeon fatigue** during long-duration operations, indirectly improving patient safety.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Features:**
 
 
• The **Mizzo Endo 4000** features a **modular design**, allowing it to be configured for various specialties such as **Urology, Gynecology, and General Surgery**.
 
• It includes **haptic feedback** mechanisms (tactile sensations) that help surgeons "feel" the tension of the tissues, a feature often missing in earlier laparoscopic tools.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Conventional Laparoscopy:**
 
 
• In **conventional laparoscopy**, the surgeon experiences the **"fulcrum effect"** (where instruments move in the opposite direction of the hand), whereas the **Mizzo Endo 4000** eliminates this, making the learning curve shorter for new surgeons.
 
• The **4K resolution** cameras provide **10x magnification**, allowing for better identification of small **nerves and blood vessels**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: In November 2025, the Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife approved several defence and paramilitary projects in which of the following protected areas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **November 2025**, the **Standing Committee of the National Board for Wildlife (SC-NBWL)** cleared several strategic **defence** and **paramilitary projects** specifically located within the **Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary**.
 
• The sanctuary is situated in the **Leh district** of the Union Territory of **Ladakh**, representing a high-altitude cold desert ecosystem of immense **geopolitical** and **ecological** importance.
 
• These approvals include the construction of **strategic roads**, **border outposts**, and **telecommunication infrastructure** to be developed by the **Border Roads Organization (BRO)** and the **Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary.***
 
• The projects aim to strengthen India's surveillance and logistics capabilities along the **Line of Actual Control (LAC)**, ensuring better troop movement and communication in the difficult terrain of **Eastern Ladakh**.
 
• The **Standing Committee**, which functions under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**, reviewed these proposals to balance **national security** requirements with the conservation needs of the region's unique biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary**:
 
 
• Established in the year **1987**, it covers an area of over **5,000 square kilometers** in **Ladakh**.
 
• It is one of the few places in **India** where the rare **Chiru (Tibetan Antelope)** is found, which is known for its fine wool called **Shahtoosh**.
 
• The sanctuary also provides a habitat for other endangered species like the **Snow Leopard**, **Tibetan Gazelle**, and the **Himalayan Ibex**.
 
 
 
• **National Board for Wildlife (NBWL)**:
 
 
• It is a **statutory body** constituted under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
• The **Prime Minister of India** serves as the **ex-officio chairperson** of the **NBWL**, while the **Union Minister of Environment** chairs the **Standing Committee**.
 
• It acts as an **advisory board** to the Central Government on framing policies and measures for **wildlife conservation**.
 
 
 
• **Other Protected Areas in Options**:
 
 
• **Dehing Patkai Wildlife Sanctuary**: Located in **Assam**, it is often referred to as the **"Amazon of the East"** due to its dense rainforest cover.
 
• **Khangchendzonga National Park**: Situated in **Sikkim**, it is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** recognized under the **"Mixed" category** for both natural and cultural significance.
 
• **Raimona National Park**: Declared as the **sixth national park** of **Assam** in **2021**, it is located in the **Kokrajhar district** and is famous for the **Golden Langur**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Infrastructure in Ladakh**:
 
 
• The government has accelerated **infrastructure development** in **Ladakh** following the **2020 border standoff** to ensure **all-weather connectivity**.
 
• The **720-km long** strategic roads and mobile towers are essential for the **Border Roads Organization (BRO)** to maintain supply lines to forward areas near the **Karakoram Pass**.
 
• **Wildlife clearances** are mandatory under **Section 29** and **Section 35** of the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** for any non-forestry activity inside a sanctuary or national park.
 
 
 
• **Conservation Challenges**:
 
 
• Large-scale construction in **high-altitude** zones can impact **migratory corridors** of wildlife and delicate **permafrost** layers.
 
• The **SC-NBWL** often imposes conditions such as **compensatory afforestation** and the creation of **wildlife passages** to mitigate the environmental footprint of **defence projects**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What does the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, prohibit unless female heirs receive their inheritance first?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dedication to Waqf**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025** (introduced as the **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024**) introduces significant reforms to the **Waqf Act, 1995**, specifically targeting the protection of **inheritance rights**.
 
• Under the new provisions, the **dedication of property to Waqf** is prohibited if such a dedication results in the deprivation of the **legal heirs**, especially **female heirs**, of their rightful **inheritance**.
 
• This amendment seeks to ensure that religious endowments do not become a tool to bypass the **succession rights** of women as guaranteed under **personal laws** or other legal frameworks. ***Hence, the statement regarding the prohibition of dedication is correct.***
 
• The Act mandates that any person intending to dedicate property as **Waqf** must have a **clear title** and ownership of the property, and they must be a **practicing Muslim** for at least **five years**.
 
• The legislation aims to bring **transparency** and **accountability** to the management of over **9 lakh hectares** of Waqf land across India, which is currently managed by various **State Waqf Boards**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Waqf Definition and Purpose**:
 
 
• **Waqf** refers to the permanent **dedication of movable or immovable property** for purposes recognized by **Muslim Law** as pious, religious, or charitable.
 
• Properties dedicated to Waqf are managed by a **Mutawalli** (manager), who acts as a supervisor rather than an owner.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Central Waqf Council**:
 
 
• The **Central Waqf Council** is a **statutory body** established in **1964** to advise the **Union Government** on matters concerning the working of **Waqf Boards**.
 
• The **2025 Amendment** proposes a more diverse composition of the Council, including the mandatory inclusion of **two women** and **two non-Muslims** to enhance inclusivity and administrative oversight.
 
 
 
• **Powers of the District Collector**:
 
 
• One of the most debated features of the **Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025** is the enhanced power given to the **District Collector**.
 
• The **Collector** now has the authority to determine whether a property claimed as **Waqf** is actually **government land**. This shifts the adjudicatory power away from the **Waqf Tribunal** in cases of land title disputes involving the state.
 
 
 
• **Registration and Portal**:
 
 
• The Act introduces a **centralized registration** process through a global **Waqf portal** to digitize records and prevent **encroachments**.
 
• Any property intended to be declared as **Waqf-alal-aulad** (Waqf for the benefit of the dedicator's family) must also ensure that the **inheritance rights** of **female heirs** are not compromised.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Abolition of 'Waqf by User'**: The **Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025** seeks to abolish the concept of **'Waqf by User'**, where a property is deemed Waqf based on long-term religious use without formal documentation. This necessitates formal **registration** for all Waqf properties.
 
• **Composition of State Waqf Boards**: The boards will now include members from diverse backgrounds, including **Shia, Sunni, Bohra, and Agakhani** communities, alongside **two non-Muslim members** and at least **two women**.
 
• **Timeline**: The **Waqf Act** was originally enacted in **1954**, significantly amended in **1995** and **2013**, and the current **2025** reforms represent the most comprehensive shift in **Waqf administration** since Independence.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following administrative bodies has been designated the nodal agency for the 'Viksit Bharat @2047' programme in 2025?

• The **Central Vigilance Commission** (CVC) is an **apex vigilance institution**, free of control from any executive authority, monitoring all vigilance activity under the Central Government, and does not function as a nodal agency for national development planning. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

__
 
• **NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• Established on **January 1, 2015**, it replaced the erstwhile **Planning Commission** to better serve the needs and aspirations of the people of India.
 
• The **Prime Minister** serves as the **Ex-officio Chairperson**. It operates on the principle of **Cooperative Federalism**, involving the active participation of State Governments in the planning process.
 
• It acts as a **think tank** providing relevant strategic and technical advice to the Centre and the States.
 
 
 
• **Viksit Bharat @2047 Goals:**
 
 
• The vision encompasses various aspects of development, including **economic growth**, social progress, **environmental sustainability**, and **good governance**.
 
• Economic targets include aiming for a **$30 trillion economy** by **2047**, with a significant increase in per capita income.
 
• The programme emphasizes **structural reforms**, digitalization, and **infrastructure development** to ensure India becomes a global leader in innovation and manufacturing.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Pillars:** The vision document prepared by **NITI Aayog** is expected to focus on **ten sectoral groups**, including **energy**, technology, **urbanization**, and social sectors like **education and health**.
 
• **Youth Engagement:** A key feature of the 2024-2025 phase is the **'Ideas Portal'**, where the youth can share their suggestions for the country's development, emphasizing the role of **Jan Bhagidari** (People's Participation).
 
• **Implementation:** The **NITI Aayog** coordinates with various **Central Ministries** and **State Governments** to align their goals with the national 2047 vision, ensuring a synchronized approach toward long-term developmental milestones.
</ul

questions.question: What is the maximum number of lenders allowed per borrower under new Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN) rules which came into effect from 1 April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN)**, which is a **Self-Regulatory Organization (SRO)** for the microfinance sector, has introduced new guidelines to address concerns of **over-indebtedness** among borrowers.
 
• According to the updated rules, the maximum number of **Microfinance (MFI) lenders** allowed per borrower has been capped at **Three**.
 
• This new regulation is scheduled to come into full effect from **April 1, 2025**, providing a transition period for the industry to align its credit assessment processes.
 
• The decision was taken to ensure that borrowers do not enter a **debt trap** by borrowing from multiple sources, a practice often referred to as **loan stacking**.
 
• Under these rules, no lender should provide a loan to a borrower who already has active loans from **three** different microfinance institutions, regardless of the loan amount or the borrower's repayment capacity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN):**
 
 
• Established in **2009**, **MFIN** is the premier industry association for the microfinance sector in India and is recognized by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** as an **SRO**.
 
• Its primary role is to ensure **responsible lending** and ethical conduct among **Non-Banking Financial Company-Microfinance Institutions (NBFC-MFIs)**.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance Loan Definition:**
 
 
• As per the **RBI Master Directions (2022)**, a microfinance loan is a **collateral-free loan** given to a household having an annual income of up to **Rs. 3 lakh**.
 
• These loans are primarily aimed at **financial inclusion** for the unbanked and underbanked population.
 
 
 
• **Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio (FOIR):**
 
 
• Besides the lender limit, the **MFIN** rules emphasize that the **FOIR** should not exceed **50%**.
 
• This means that the total monthly loan repayment obligations of a household must not exceed **50%** of its **monthly income**.
 
 
 
• **Credit Information Companies (CICs):**
 
 
• Lenders are mandated to check the credit history of potential borrowers through **CICs** like **Equifax, Experian, or CIBIL** to verify the number of existing active lenders before sanctioning new credit.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Harmony:** The **RBI** introduced a harmonized regulatory framework in **March 2022**, which removed the **interest rate cap** but shifted the focus toward a **risk-based pricing** model and **protection against over-leveraging**.
 
• **Implementation Timeline:** While the **SRO** issued these "guardrails" in late **2024**, the mandatory enforcement of the **three-lender limit** begins on the **1st of April, 2025**.
 
• **Industry Impact:** This move is expected to slow down **asset growth** for some aggressive lenders but will significantly improve the **asset quality** and sustainability of the microfinance ecosystem in the long run.
</ul

questions.question: The National Red List Roadmap, launched in October 2025, primarily aims at which of the following?

options.text: To monitor air and water pollution levels across industrial zones
To track progress on renewable energy adoption and emissions reduction
To develop renewable energy targets for environmental sustainability
To assess and monitor the conservation status of the country's flora and fauna

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To assess and monitor the conservation status of the country's flora and fauna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Red List Roadmap** was officially launched in **October 2025** as a strategic initiative to systematically evaluate the extinction risk of species within the country.
 
• Its primary objective is to align national conservation efforts with the **International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)** standards to provide a clear picture of the **conservation status** of **flora and fauna**.
 
• The roadmap serves as a guiding document for the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** to prioritize species that require immediate protection and habitat restoration.
 
• It facilitates the creation of a comprehensive **National Red List**, which acts as a critical tool for policymakers to allocate funds and resources toward **biodiversity hotspots** and threatened ecosystems. ***Hence, the correct answer is option (4).***
 
• The launch coincided with global efforts to meet the **2030 targets** of the **Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework**, emphasizing the reduction of species extinction rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **IUCN Red List Categories:**
 
 
• The **IUCN** classifies species into nine groups, including **Extinct (EX)**, **Critically Endangered (CR)**, **Endangered (EN)**, and **Vulnerable (VU)**.
 
• The **National Red List Roadmap** utilizes these global criteria but tailors them to the **regional and national context** of the country's unique biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Involved Organizations:**
 
 
• The **Zoological Survey of India (ZSI)**, established in **1916**, and the **Botanical Survey of India (BSI)**, established in **1890**, are the lead technical agencies responsible for data collection.
 
• These organizations conduct extensive field surveys and **DNA barcoding** to accurately identify and catalog species for the roadmap.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework in India:**
 
 
• The initiative supports the **Biological Diversity Act, 2002**, which aims at the conservation of biological resources and equitable sharing of benefits.
 
• It also complements the **Wildlife Protection Act, 1972**, by providing scientific data to update the various **Schedules** that define the legal protection levels for different animals and plants.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF):** The roadmap is a direct response to **Target 4** of the **Kunming-Montreal GBF**, which mandates urgent management actions to halt human-induced extinction of known threatened species.
 
• **Data Integration:** The roadmap emphasizes the use of **Geographic Information Systems (GIS)** and **Remote Sensing** to track changes in species distribution and habitat loss over time.
 
• **Endemism:** A special focus is placed on **Endemic species** found in regions like the **Western Ghats**, the **Himalayas**, and the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**, as these species are found nowhere else in the world and are highly susceptible to climate change.
 
• **Role of the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA):** The **NBA**, headquartered in **Chennai**, plays a pivotal role in ensuring that the roadmap's implementation adheres to the **Nagoya Protocol** on access and benefit-sharing.
</ul
